text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- New stock exchange legislation reveals corporate insiders' personal share ownership for first time.
- Merita Bank board members have lightened personal holdings in UPM-Kymmene in past six months. One board member sold over 280,000 shares, others altogether 3,350 shares.
- Sunday schools are making a come-back in Finland. @
- Snow sculptors began crafting snow church at Helsinki's Senate Square.
- Real estate association continues efforts to ban sales of spray paint to under 15 year-olds.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Hamburgers becoming a billion-markka business. Three leading hamburger restaurant chains plan to increase sales 20 to 30 percent this year.
- London analysts upbeat on Pohjola life- insurance restructuring plan, say they expect it to buy Pohjola shares of associate Suomi in two or three years and cancel them. @
- Brokers say average price-earnings ratio of Helsinki-listed stocks last year, 16, approached that of European shares, 17.6.
- Renault's Renault Vehicule Industrie says Partek's merger with Sisu Oy will not affect its joint venture with Sisu.
DEMARI
SAK trade federation chief Lauri Ihalainen voiced strong support for Social Democratic Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen and for Lipponen government economic policy. @
AAMULEHTI
- Minister for European Affairs Ole Norrback rejects suggestion that bigger states in the EU should have more decision-making powers.
- Studies show new anti-depressant drugs can help people get through the dark months of the year at northern latitudes.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Central criminal police are investigating six attempts by computer hackers to break into business and university information networks. @
- Turku's TPS ice-hockey team won the European league championship, beating Moscow's Dynamo five goals to two in front of a home crowd.
